### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e253f3ab09717234fedae8e4d7a193cd1a12b0da` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9ae6fc895624857d4ccc8079d9e892adb8b25319` — the merge of head `e090be93463b7273a813ee3cdfcb2c7863d6619b` into base `e253f3ab09717234fedae8e4d7a193cd1a12b0da`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9ae6fc895624857d4ccc8079d9e892adb8b25319 && git checkout 9ae6fc895624857d4ccc8079d9e892adb8b25319
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e253f3ab09717234fedae8e4d7a193cd1a12b0da e090be93463b7273a813ee3cdfcb2c7863d6619b && git checkout -B drift-repro e253f3ab09717234fedae8e4d7a193cd1a12b0da && git merge --no-ff e090be93463b7273a813ee3cdfcb2c7863d6619b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e253f3ab09717234fedae8e4d7a193cd1a12b0da
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e090be93463b7273a813ee3cdfcb2c7863d6619b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts, docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md + none

Inputs read: card #31592 (body, triage 6724356074, unblock 6730608741, claim 6731116574, dev report 6731804928), PR #31786 (body, 5-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the 67 check-runs on the head (every non-skipped run `success`: Test Core 1-8, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Build Docs, Build Core; the skipped ones are opt-in or matrix placeholders). The remainder of the diff (`type-compat.test.ts`, `external-datasources.mdx`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; it is read here only where it pins or restates what the two `hits` files say.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set widened — `isCompatible('RAW(16)', 'lookup' | 'master_detail' | 'user', 'oracle')`: `'lossy'` → `true`.** Right. Judged against the live driver on `main`, not the PR body: a comparison comparand on a catalog-reported `RAW(16)` field binds `HEXTORAW(?)` in `sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts` `coerceFilterValue` L181-188, with the refusal of non-uuid text in the bare-equality branch (L635-637), the operator-object branch (L899-901) and the second equality branch (L1094-1096); a written value binds through `formatInput` (`sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts` L263-277, role `'write'`); the by-id key binds in `update` (`sql-driver-sequence-semantics.ts` L294), `delete`/`bulkDelete` (`sql-driver-bulk-operations.ts` L279-280) and the post-insert read-back (`sql-driver-crud.ts` L450-454). Lookup expansion reads the target as `{ id: { $in: ids } }` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts` L593), the comparand path. The oracle pins (`sql-driver-oracle-dialect.test.ts` L391-470, L473-530) hold each of these shapes. So a reference field over a `SYS_GUID()` key is filtered, written, keyed and resolved by the string it reads: the pairing the matrix now calls exact is the one the runtime honours.
2. **Accept-set held — `isCompatible('RAW(16)', 'text', 'oracle')` stays `'lossy'`.** Right. `assertOracleUuidComparand` judges only `ORACLE_EMPTY_STRING_SENSITIVE_OPERATORS` (the comparison set) and `coerceFilterValue` leaves a non-uuid value alone, so `$contains: 'abc'` compiles `"ACCT_REF" LIKE ? ESCAPE ?` against the RAW with no conversion (control pin L434-438). Oracle converts the RAW to its hex text, so a fragment of the read-back string with a hyphen matches no row and raises nothing. A `text` field's operators are the pattern set (list search is an `$or` of `$icontains`, `search-filter.ts` L206-208), so `'lossy'` is the honest answer and the draft's `// REVIEW:` marker stays (service-datasource L957: the suggested type for `RAW(16)` is `text`).
3. **Accept-set unchanged elsewhere.** `number` over `RAW(16)` stays `false` (new pin): the demotion list can only move an EXACT pairing to `'lossy'`, never promote. Other `RAW` widths stay `binary`; postgres `uuid`/`lookup` stays `true`; `mssql`/`text` `addLossy` is untouched. `DIALECT_LOSSY_RULES` is still "only ever toward `'lossy'`", as the ADR sentence says.
4. **Public surface.** No export changes. `DialectLossyRule` is module-private (no `export` on the interface), `Compatibility`, `isCompatible`, `canonicalizeSqlType` and `suggestFieldTypeForSqlType` keep their signatures. The published change is the matrix's ANSWER, which is why ② is on the metadata-protocol axis.
5. **Consumers on `main`** (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts`): `validateObject` L1339-1356 stops emitting the `severity: 'warning'` `type_mismatch` for the three reference types over an oracle `RAW(16)` column and keeps it for `text`; the draft path L957 is unchanged (judges the suggested type, `text`); the `!== true` lookup gate L1113 lives in `draftLookups`, which iterates `navigationCandidates(table)` (OData navigations) — and were a SQL foreign key ever to reach it, drafting a `RAW(16)` key as a `lookup` is exactly the widening this card declares. No pin in service-datasource holds the old `'lossy'` answer (swept `packages/services`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/runtime`, `packages/cli`: zero `RAW(16)` / `demoteExact` hits), consistent with the green consumer suite in CI.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31592-oracle-raw16-reference-exact.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, carrying `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`; the PR body carries the same two lines. The diff moves `packages/spec/src/**` and changes the meaning of a published answer (`'lossy'` → `true` for three pairings), which is the `semantic` kind, and the level rule (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: `added` / `narrowed` / `semantic` → at least one moved package at `minor` or above) accepts `minor` on the moved package. `Check Changeset` on the head is `success`. No `!` in the title, no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner owed. Right.

**Clause-②:** `yes (widening)` — correct: three pairings move from `'lossy'` to exact, and nothing is taken away. The changeset's reader-facing text matches the code: the validation warning goes for the three types, `text` keeps its warning and the draft's review marker, other dialects and other `RAW` widths are unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6731804928: `open_questions: []`; four `deviations`; one `out_of_scope_findings` entry. The brief flagged one deviation. Each is answered here:

1. **Narrowed, not dropped (`demoteExact` becomes a `FieldType[]`; oracle/uuid names `text` only).** Accepted. The card's task line allows "or narrow it", and the narrowing is the only honest shape: dropping the rule would have declared `text` exact while `$contains` on the column still matches hex text and not the string a read returns (control pin, `sql-driver-oracle-dialect.test.ts` L434). The card's "the pairing must not be declared before the runtime honours it" is met for the three types lifted and respected for the one kept.
2. **ADR-0015 §4.6 `DIALECT_LOSSY_RULES` sentence ("oracle demotes the exact pairings of `uuid`") also corrected.** Accepted. The claim named L431-434 and the `Amended by` line; the extra sentence is in the same section and the change made it false. An ADR left saying "the exact pairings" over a table that now names one pairing would have been a contract defect, so this is the edit the card owed, not scope creep.
3. **`spec` `test:repo` not run locally.** Covered by the head's `Test Core` runs (`success`).
4. **Live Oracle NOT MEASURED.** Accepted with the risk named: the lift rests on the #31390 compiled-SQL pins and on Oracle's documented implicit `RAW`-to-character conversion, exactly the evidence #31390 itself landed on (its live conformance cell is also unmeasured in CI). This record does not weigh it heavier than #31390 did; it is a known gap of the driver bind, not of the matrix answer, and the matrix answer is the thing under review.
5. **Out-of-scope observation: `CANONICAL_TO_FIELD.uuid` keeps `user` exact on every dialect, yet a platform user id is never a uuid.** Answered, not escalated as a defect of this PR. The base row's own comment (type-compat.ts L295-306) documents the measurement: better-auth mints a 32-character string and the SQL driver a 16-character nanoid, and the `uuid` row keeps `user` because a caller-supplied id is stored verbatim. With this PR oracle joins postgres and mssql in that judgement; the driver bind refuses a non-uuid write with `VALIDATION_ERROR` and a non-uuid comparand with `INVALID_FILTER`, so nothing is corrupted — the pairing is honoured at the binding and simply never fits a minted platform id. That is the base row's question on every dialect, the card names `lookup` / `master_detail`, and `user` rides along only because narrowing to `text` is the honest list. Graded a nit below; it belongs on a follow-up card against the `uuid` base row, not on this head.

No ruling on the card is contradicted. Triage's lane and grade (`domain:spec`, p3, metadata-protocol change under #31424 rule 2) match what landed. The claim's file surface (`type-compat.ts` + test, the mdx rows, ADR §4.6 + `Amended by`, a changeset, no `driver-sql` code) is exactly the five files in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts`** — judged against ADR-0015 §4.6 (the ruling it implements) and its first consumer (`validateObject`), and against the driver it describes.

- *Shape.* `readonly demoteExact?: readonly FieldType[]` with `rule?.demoteExact?.includes(fieldType) ? 'lossy' : true` is the minimal change that keeps the table's invariant (a dialect only ever moves toward `'lossy'`) and keeps the member live (oracle still uses it). `demoteExact: []` demotes nothing, and the dev's two ablations (flag reading restored; empty list) each turn one pin red, so the new pin set discriminates both halves. Nothing is promoted: the list is consulted only inside the `entry.exact.includes(fieldType)` branch. Holds.
- *Sentence-by-sentence against the driver.* "reads a `RAW(16)` column as a lower-case hyphenated UUID string" — `oracleRaw16AsUuid`. "binds a comparison comparand, a written value and a by-id key for it as `HEXTORAW(?)` over that string's hex digits" — `oracleUuidRawBinding` (`HEXTORAW(?)` over `value.replace(/-/g, '').toUpperCase()`), reached from the three sites in ①.1. "A reference field over it … is filtered, written and resolved by the very string it reads" — pins L392-426, L474-530, plus expansion's `$in`. "its pattern operators … are not bound through `HEXTORAW`, so they match the column as the text Oracle converts a `RAW` to (its 32 hex digits, upper case, no hyphens)" — control pin L434-438; `assertOracleUuidComparand` skips the pattern set by design. Each sentence has code behind it.
- *Tried to break it.* `$ne` / `$nin` keep their null-safe shape around the bound comparand (pin L416-420); `$in` with mixed-case members binds every member (L404-408); the range operators are in the comparison set and bind; `null` stays `IS NULL`; a `master_detail` cascade is a `deleteMany` whose FK comparand binds; `create` without an id mints a nanoid (`sql-driver-crud.ts` L287-291) which `formatInput` then refuses with `VALIDATION_ERROR` — a refusal, never a silent write; a failed catalog read falls back to binding text (Oracle then errors loudly, the #31390 posture). A `VARCHAR2` column holding uuids is still text (the column decides, never the value; pins L428-432, L440-444). None of these breaks the lifted pairings.
- **Finding F1 — nit (prose face).** The docblock's closing clause, "a fragment of that string with a hyphen, or in the case it is read in, answers no row instead of a refusal", is overbroad for the folding operators: `$icontains` / `$ilike` compile `LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER(?)` (`sql-driver-predicate-emitters.ts` `textMatchPredicate`), so a lower-case, hyphen-free fragment of the read-back string DOES match under them. The test comment and the mdx bullet say it precisely ("matches only when it has no hyphen and the operator ignores case"); the jsdoc should say the same. No effect on the matrix's answer or the contract; fix on the prose face in a later round or leave as an accepted deviation.
- **Finding F2 — nit (follow-up card).** `user` is lifted with the two reference types because `text` is the only pairing the driver half-serves. The base row's `user`-under-`uuid` judgement (③.5) is the pre-existing question on every dialect; with this PR oracle stops warning about it for the wrong reason. Recommend a follow-up card on `CANONICAL_TO_FIELD.uuid` (does a `user` field, fixed to `sys_user`, ever belong in a uuid column's exact set?). Not this card's head.
- **Finding F3 — nit (follow-up or accepted deviation).** `$search` over a `lookup` named in `searchFields`: `fieldClausesForTerm` emits `$icontains` for reference types (they pass the text-operator door as record-id strings), so a search term that is a fragment of a `RAW(16)` lookup's id matches only when hyphen-free. This is the same silent-no-row shape the docblock already names for `text`, on a path no caller uses to resolve a reference (references are filtered by equality or membership, which bind). No effect on the lifted pairings' contract.

**`docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md`** — judged against its first consumer (`type-compat.ts` + `validateObject`) and its execution plan.

- §4.6 `RAW(16)` sentence now states the bind (comparison, write, by-id key — the three roles the driver has), names #31390 as the source, declares `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` exact and `text` `'lossy'` with the pattern-operator reason: identical to what `DIALECT_LOSSY_RULES` and the jsdoc say, and to what `validateObject` now emits. §4.6's `DIALECT_LOSSY_RULES` sentence ("demotes the exact `text` pairing of `uuid`") matches the one-element list. The `Amended by` entry is dated, names the card and the section, and follows the form of the #31328 / #31327 entries beside it. §11 P2 places the type-compat matrix in the rollout and §16.1 asks for its unit tests; `type-compat.test.ts` pins the new answers and the `Spec property liveness` / `Test Core` runs are green. The ADR's §4.6 claim about `isCompatible`'s shape (`boolean | 'lossy'`) is unchanged and still true. No finding.

**Implementing files in the diff apart from `hits`:** none. `type-compat.ts` is both the schema face and the code the ADR sentence describes; the test, the mdx and the changeset are the lane seat's remainder.

Findings: F1 nit, F2 nit, F3 nit. No must-fix, no should-fix: nits alone end the round.

Rendered by the seat's isolated child session `9f9f0eb5-2885-550b-8927-ffc7a5154621` (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID); the seat below adopts and posts the verdict.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-h15c0w`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jUe9c6YdtNkrzUnMUd`

**VERDICT: PASS**

_Seat adoption note: read before adopting. Spot-checked the pattern-operator premise (`coerceFilterValue` binds only uuid comparands; a pattern operator's text is never bound through `HEXTORAW`) and F1's fold path (`textMatchPredicate` takes a `fold` flag). Adopted as rendered. F1 to F3 are accepted nits._

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：Oracle 外部数据源里 `RAW(16)`（`SYS_GUID()`）列上的 `lookup`、`master_detail`、`user` 字段，类型兼容表从「有损」改回「完全兼容」，对象校验不再为此告警；`text` 字段仍判有损，草稿仍标记复核。ADR-0015 §4.6 和外部数据源文档同步改写。
- 为什么改：#31390（PR #31642）已让驱动按 `HEXTORAW(?)` 绑定这类列的比较值、写入值和按 id 定位，引用字段按读回的 uuid 字符串就能过滤、写入、解析；而 `text` 的模糊匹配（`$contains`、`$like` 等）没有经过 `HEXTORAW`，仍会静默查不到，所以只放宽三种引用类型。
- 风险与回滚：只放宽不收紧，其他方言、其他 `RAW` 宽度的答案不变；没有导出变化，不改驱动代码。回滚 = revert 本 PR。真实 Oracle 未实测，依据与 #31390 相同（编译后的 SQL 断言）。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts` 的 `DIALECT_LOSSY_RULES`（`demoteExact` 改为字段类型列表，oracle/uuid 只降级 `text`）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/type-compat.test.ts` 全绿。
- 需要你做的：批准本 PR（Tier H，因改了 `docs/adr/0015`）；批准后由本席落地。契约复核 PASS 在案：评论 6732289043，`Head-sha: e090be93463b7273a813ee3cdfcb2c7863d6619b`。
- 席位意见：建议合。CI 全绿，契约复核只有 3 条 nit、无须改动。分支落后 main 12 个提交，`git merge-tree` 无冲突，合并队列会在最新 main 上重建验证，所以不为合 main 移动已复核的 head。

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · 2026-11-09T04:31Z · head `e090be93463b7273a813ee3cdfcb2c7863d6619b`

Seat `domain:spec#2` reviewed the diff of its own dispatch (claim 6731116574 on #31592, card thread `session_01QsR2jULf9M1RFFq4dq9ioH`, report 6731804928). Checked against GitHub, not against the report.

1. **Shape:** 5 files, +67 / -27. Draft, base `main`, body opens `Fixes #31592`. `type-compat.ts` + test, `external-datasources.mdx`, ADR-0015 §4.6 + its `Amended by` line, one changeset (`@objectstack/spec` minor). Every file is inside the claim. No `driver-sql` change.
2. **Premise:** held at claim time (43fb4822) and on this head: `oracle: { uuid: { demoteExact: true } }` demoted every exact uuid pairing; the #31390 bind (PR #31642, 836d408f) is on main and binds comparands, writes and by-id keys, but not pattern-operator text (`coerceFilterValue`).
3. **Gates / check-runs:** on this head 67 runs, 57 success, 10 skipped, 0 red. `check-expected-skips --pr 31786`: OK (exit 0, roster pinned to main's tip). Dev: `dispatch-gates --ran` 108 derived, 107 exit 0, 1 NOT MEASURED locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, full build; green in CI); spec 824 files and service-datasource 74 files green; two ablations each red.
4. **Accepted deviations:** the lift is narrowed, not dropped (`demoteExact` becomes `FieldType[]`, oracle/uuid keeps `text`), as the brief allowed ("lift only what is honoured"). The extra ADR-0015 §4.6 sentence on `DIALECT_LOSSY_RULES` was made false by this change and is corrected in the same section. Live Oracle is not measured, which is the same evidence base as #31390. The contract review's three nits stand. F1: the jsdoc's "in the case it is read in" is overbroad for the folding operators; the test and the mdx say it precisely. F2: `user` under the `uuid` base row is a pre-existing question on every dialect. F3: `$search` over a `RAW(16)` lookup id fragment matches only when it is hyphen-free.
5. **Out of scope:** `text` over `RAW(16)` stays `'lossy'` until pattern operators bind; that belongs to the driver, not to this card. Consumers: `validateObject` drops the warning for the three reference types; the draft's `// REVIEW:` marker (suggested type `text`) is unchanged.
6. **Landing:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31786`: governed, Tier H (`docs/adr/**` ×1). `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`: PASS, record 6732289043 on this head (an isolated Fable reviewer adopted by this seat, under the maintainer's 2026-11-08 16:12Z rule). The maintainer merges by hand, or an authorized approval (`GOVERNED_APPROVERS`) and then this seat lands it (ready, auto-merge). On merge: `Fixes` closes #31592; this seat posts the landing note.
